items.title: Share canonical host-verdict binding derivation
items.context: Extract the keyId, validationDigest, and promptDigest derivation currently private to quorum submission into a shared fail-closed helper while preserving quorum semantics.

happy.desc: Golden-vector logic test calls the extracted shared derivation helper and the pre-extraction quorum derivation oracle with identical canonical storyId, headHash, materialDigest, storyFilesHash, testEvidence, hostId, provider, sessionId, and keyId; keyId, validationDigest, and promptDigest must be byte-for-byte equal.

Quorum integration smoke submits the same valid two-independent-host, current-reviewer-pass fixture before and after delegation to the shared helper and proves the public lattice.quorum_submit.v1 result, verdict count/run ids, stored binding fields, and gate-counted assurance outcome are unchanged.

edge.desc: Canonical vectors cover both present and absent optional headHash plus present and unreadable/missing test evidence; validationDigest stays deterministic and exactly matches the existing canonicalDigest envelope for each case rather than silently dropping or inventing fields.

Regression assertions pin validation schemaVersion lattice.quorum_submit.validation_digest.v1, prompt schemaVersion lattice.quorum_submit.prompt_digest.v1, and purpose local voluntary 3x2 review quorum after signed reviewer passes, so extraction or reuse cannot drift the digest namespace or semantic purpose.

adversarial.desc: The shared helper fails closed and emits no usable bindings when required canonical identity or freshness inputs are empty/invalid, including storyId, materialDigest, storyFilesHash, hostId, provider, sessionId, or keyId; callers cannot obtain a gate-counting digest from partial/defaulted data.

Replay/collision tests vary one of storyId, headHash or testEvidence, materialDigest, storyFilesHash, hostId, provider, sessionId, and keyId at a time and prove the affected canonical digest changes; quorum still rejects hosts sharing normalized hostId, sessionId, or keyId and never collapses 3x2 independence through the refactor.

items.title: Add explicit single-host binding derivation mode
items.context: Allow autopilot_review_submit to derive current canonical bindings only when explicitly requested; reject supplied stale or inconsistent bindings and never invent a second host.

happy.desc: With the explicit single-host binding-derivation mode enabled and a current story/evidence snapshot plus one real host identity supplied, autopilot_review_submit derives keyId, validationDigest, and promptDigest through the canonical shared derivation, accepts the submission, and persists exactly one verdict whose bindings equal the canonical values for the same inputs.

edge.desc: Without the explicit derivation flag, autopilot_review_submit preserves the legacy contract: it does not synthesize missing bindings, retains the existing warning or acceptance behavior for legacy callers, and does not silently opt the caller into derived bindings.

A valid explicit-derivation submission records only the single supplied host identity and one verdict; it creates no second host, independence claim, quorum verdict, Authority receipt, or assurance stronger than degraded-single-host.

adversarial.desc: When explicit derivation is requested but any caller-supplied keyId, validationDigest, or promptDigest conflicts with the current canonical derived value, the command fails closed before persistence; a before-and-after verdict-state comparison proves no verdict or partial artifact was written.

When story material, story-files binding, validation evidence, or required host identity is stale, missing, or inconsistent at submission time, explicit derivation fails before write rather than deriving from stale evidence or accepting caller assertions; existing verdict state remains logically unchanged.

items.title: Align fallback guidance and regression coverage
items.context: Emit an executable degraded single-host command and cover valid three-round use, stale rejection, legacy warning behavior, and unchanged quorum behavior.
